html:
The Guane were a Chibchan-speaking people of the canyon country of the Chicamocha and Suárez rivers, in today's Santander department of Colombia. Their neighbours to the south were the Muisca, with whom they traded.

They farmed maize, cotton and other crops, and were known for their fine cotton cloth, which they traded widely. Spanish conquerors entered their land from about 1540 and founded the town of Vélez nearby. Within a century disease, forced labour and mixing had ended the Guane as a separate people of Spanish America. The village of Guane in Barichara keeps their name and a museum of their pottery and remains. See also Colombia.
